title: Hipobuy Spreadsheet Links Not Working: Checks and Alternatives
description: Check a broken Hipobuy spreadsheet link, distinguish a missing listing from an unavailable option, and compare alternatives without ordering the wrong item.
dek: Check a broken Hipobuy spreadsheet link, distinguish a missing listing from an unavailable option, and compare alternatives without ordering the wrong item.

sections.heading: Identify the link that actually failed
paragraphs: A Hipobuy spreadsheet can contain several different kinds of links. A category opens a group of products, a catalogue entry describes one item, a seller listing contains selectable options, and an agent order page adds purchasing details. When something does not open, first identify which of these steps failed. A broken catalogue shortcut does not prove that the seller removed the product. An unavailable seller listing does not prove that every product in that category has disappeared. This distinction saves time and reduces the risk of paying for an unrelated replacement.

Write down the page address, product name, displayed product ID and the exact message you can see. A screenshot is useful when it includes the option you selected and the date. Keep account details and payment information out of screenshots shared publicly. On this directory, product buttons open a separate catalogue, while guides remain here. The destination is a place to verify the current item; a historical row is not an order confirmation or a guarantee of availability. Start with the relevant category when you cannot identify the original item confidently.

sections.heading: Separate a page problem from an option problem
paragraphs: Read the destination before deciding that a link is dead. A listing may open normally while one colour, size or quantity is unavailable. It may also show a starting price for an option that differs from the product in the thumbnail. Record the selected options rather than comparing only the main image. If the page works but your required size does not, your next decision concerns a different size or another product, not a technical repair to the link.

A blank page, an explicit not-found response, a login screen and a platform restriction are different situations. Use the normal sign-in flow where an account is required. Do not enter credentials into an unfamiliar page reached through a shortened link. If the service says an item is restricted, ask its support team about the applicable rules rather than trying to evade the restriction. A temporary loading problem can justify a later retry, but repeated reloading cannot restore a product the seller has actually removed. Preserve the original identifier while investigating.

sections.heading: Recover the original product information
paragraphs: Return to the spreadsheet row and collect the useful evidence that still exists: the title, original product ID, category, images and any saved size chart. Remove accidental spaces from a copied address, but do not guess a different product number. Two addresses with similar numbers can describe completely different items. If a shared message shortened the URL or omitted the final characters, obtain the full link from the original source instead of constructing a replacement that merely looks plausible.

Use this site's search with the product name or ID to look for a matching catalogue entry. Compare more than one feature before treating a result as the same product. The same stock photograph can appear in multiple listings, and one seller can list several versions of a similar item. Match the source identifier when it is available, then inspect colour, construction, included pieces and selectable options. If those details do not align, call the result an alternative. It is more useful to acknowledge an alternative than to imply that a different item is the original.

sections.heading: Compare alternatives with a small decision record
paragraphs: Create a short record for each candidate: destination, date checked, selected version, size, item price, domestic delivery and unresolved questions. Limit your shortlist to a few genuinely comparable items. A long list of unverified tabs makes it easy to mix one item's price with another item's photographs. When a catalogue card contains several styles, save the chosen option as well as the parent listing. A seller's general rating cannot tell you whether that particular option will fit or arrive as pictured.

For example, imagine that your saved hoodie is unavailable in medium. Candidate A has the same print but a different chest measurement. Candidate B has a similar cut but different fabric information. Neither is an exact replacement merely because the photographs look close. Compare the dimensions against a garment that fits, check the current return conditions, and decide which uncertainty matters most. This is an illustrative comparison, not a recommendation of a particular seller. Keep any difference visible in your notes so it is not forgotten when you later inspect warehouse photos.

sections.heading: Check the full price before replacing an order
paragraphs: A cheap alternative can change the total cost in ways the spreadsheet does not show. The selected option may cost more than the starting price. Domestic delivery, optional inspection, payment costs and international shipping may be separate. A bulkier replacement can increase packed volume even if its listed weight is similar. Compare the complete expected purchase rather than treating a lower item price as a guaranteed saving. Do this before ordering when a change is easiest to make.

If an existing order is still pending, establish whether it can be cancelled before placing a second order. A page disappearing after payment does not by itself mean that the original order was cancelled or refunded. Save the order number, payment record and seller status. Ask for a specific clarification: whether the selected item was purchased, whether the seller dispatched it, or whether a refund has been initiated. The applicable response depends on the actual service and seller terms. Avoid duplicate purchases made simply because the first page stopped loading.

sections.heading: Use warehouse evidence to confirm the replacement
paragraphs: Once a replacement arrives at the warehouse, compare it with its own saved order details. Do not approve it against photographs from the unavailable original. Confirm the version, colour and label, then inspect the measurements and visible condition relevant to that category. Shoes need views of both items and useful size evidence. Clothing benefits from a flat measurement with clear endpoints. Bags need dimensions, closures and included accessories checked. Request the missing evidence that would actually change your decision.

A successful page load is only a technical check. It does not establish authenticity, material composition, durability or seller reliability. Likewise, a warehouse image cannot demonstrate long-term comfort or the quality of hidden components. Keep these limits separate from visible facts. If the received variation is wrong, document the difference and contact the relevant service within its current window. The storage period advertised by an agent is not automatically the seller's return period. Resolving the item before international dispatch usually leaves more practical choices than discovering the mismatch after delivery.

sections.heading: Keep a shortlist that remains useful later
paragraphs: After checking a link, record what you actually verified and when. Useful labels include page opened, selected size available, measurement requested and replacement required. Avoid a permanent verified label that hides the age or scope of the check. If you share your shortlist, include that context. Someone else may be shopping on a different date, in a different country or for a different variation. Your successful purchase cannot guarantee their result, and a historical price is not a current quotation.

Finish the process with a clean path: return to the category, open one candidate, confirm the exact options, estimate the complete cost, and preserve the order details for QC. Save a second candidate only if it addresses a real uncertainty. This approach makes a broken Hipobuy spreadsheet link a manageable research problem. It also prevents the more expensive mistake of opening a working link and assuming it must describe the product you originally wanted. The goal is a traceable choice, supported by current details, before money or an international parcel is committed.

title: Hipobuy Hoodie Size Guide: Measurements, Fit and QC
description: Compare hoodie chest width, body length, shoulders and sleeves with a garment you own, then use warehouse measurements to check your selected size.
dek: Compare hoodie chest width, body length, shoulders and sleeves with a garment you own, then use warehouse measurements to check your selected size.

sections.heading: Start with a hoodie that already fits
paragraphs: A useful Hipobuy hoodie size guide begins with a garment, not a universal instruction to size up. Choose a hoodie or sweatshirt whose fit you understand. Decide whether you want to repeat that fit or change something specific, such as body length, sleeve coverage or space for layers. Different listings can use the same size letter for noticeably different cuts. The familiar letter on the label is therefore a reference, while the actual measurements provide a stronger basis for comparison.

Lay your reference garment on a flat surface and smooth ordinary wrinkles without pulling the fabric tight. Close a zipper if the seller's measurement method does so. Use a flexible tape and record the unit beside every figure. Keep photographs of the measuring points so you can repeat the method later. A measurement taken after washing may differ from the garment when new; record that context too. The purpose is not to predict every detail of fit from a table. It is to replace an untested size assumption with a small set of observations you can compare.
Keep this reference record with your shortlist so each later comparison uses the same garment, units and measuring points.

sections.heading: Distinguish body measurements from garment measurements
paragraphs: Check what the seller's size chart measures. A body chart describes the person the garment is intended to fit. A garment chart describes the item itself. These are not interchangeable, because clothing normally includes space between the body and the fabric. Nike's official men's tops chart, for example, explicitly identifies its numbers as body measurements. That explains the distinction; it does not make Nike's chart the correct chart for every hoodie listed in a third-party catalogue.

Flat chest width is usually a straight measurement across a laid-flat garment at a specified point. A body chest measurement goes around the torso. Doubling a flat width may help describe a simple garment's approximate circumference at that line, but it does not establish a recommended body size or account for all shaping. Ask which method a seller uses if the chart is unclear. Compare garment to garment and body to body. Mixing the two can produce a confident-looking calculation that selects the wrong size.

sections.heading: Record the measurements that affect your fit
paragraphs: Chest width helps assess room through the torso, while body length affects where the hem sits. Shoulder and sleeve measurements help explain arm coverage, but construction matters. A dropped shoulder can move the sleeve's starting seam down the arm. A raglan sleeve may be measured from a different starting point altogether. Read the chart's diagram instead of assuming that every sleeve number starts at the same seam. Record front and back length separately when the design has a noticeably uneven hem.

Also inspect the opening and shape of the garment. A narrow ribbed hem can sit differently from a straight open hem despite a similar chest width. A heavy hood, cropped body or boxy cut can affect how the garment hangs. Numbers describe part of this, while clear front, back and side photographs provide additional context. Material and weight claims belong to the listing unless independently tested. Do not infer fabric composition, warmth or shrinkage from a stock photograph. For your decision, identify which measurement would make the garment unusable and verify that one first.

sections.heading: Work through a comparison without guessing a size
paragraphs: Consider an illustrative reference hoodie with a flat chest width of 58 cm and a body length of 68 cm. A candidate listed at 60 cm across the chest and 66 cm long is wider but shorter. That difference cannot be summarized accurately as simply larger. If your main concern is sleeve length or coverage below the waist, the additional chest width may not solve it. These example numbers are not a size recommendation and do not describe any product in the catalogue.

Build a small comparison with four columns: measurement, reference garment, candidate garment and difference. Add the seller's stated measurement tolerance if one is provided, without inventing a standard allowance. Check whether the endpoints match before subtracting values. If you fall between two options, describe the trade-off in ordinary terms: more torso room, a longer body or a different sleeve position. Do not automatically choose the larger label. Compare the exact cuts and the return conditions, then select the option that addresses the fit you actually want.

sections.heading: Request useful warehouse measurement photos
paragraphs: After the item arrives, confirm its colour, selected version and size label before measuring. A perfectly clear tape photograph of the wrong variation does not answer your question. Ask for a flat, un-stretched measurement with the tape's starting point and end point visible. Name the requested dimension rather than asking only for better QC. A chest-width photograph and a body-length photograph are more actionable than a general request to check the size. Use the same method as your reference garment where possible.

Perspective can distort a photograph. An angled tape, a hidden zero point or fabric folded under itself can make the number hard to interpret. Ask for clarification when the uncertainty would change your decision, rather than treating a blurry image as a precise result. Check both sleeves if visible asymmetry is a concern. Allow for the fact that a photograph measures the garment in one position; it does not simulate wearing it. Compare the evidence to your requirements and the seller's stated dimensions, while keeping any unresolved discrepancy explicit.

sections.heading: Combine fit checks with visible construction checks
paragraphs: Fit is only one part of the warehouse decision. Inspect front and back views, the hood, cuffs, hem, pocket openings and any zipper. Compare print or embroidery placement with the selected listing option. Look for visible stains, pulls, open seams or uneven edges. Lighting can alter colour, so a small colour difference in one photograph should prompt a clearer reference rather than an immediate claim of a defect. Ask for a close-up of a specific area when necessary.

Pictures cannot establish every quality claim. They will not reliably prove fibre content, long-term durability or how the hoodie feels against your skin. Nor can they guarantee how much it will change after washing. Follow the actual care label and avoid assuming a particular treatment will make an unsuitable size fit. If the measurements or variation are materially wrong, keep the evidence and check the live exchange or return procedure before international shipping. Storage time and return eligibility are separate conditions, and optional inspection services may have their own charges.

sections.heading: Make the final choice before packing
paragraphs: Once the fit and visible condition meet your requirements, record why you approved the item. Save the product identifier, selected size, measurement photographs and date. This record is useful if you later compare another hoodie or investigate a mismatch. If several items are waiting in the warehouse, mark each separately as approved, awaiting measurements or requiring action. One acceptable hoodie should not cause you to approve an entire mixed parcel without inspecting the remaining pieces.

Consider packing after the item decision. Soft garments may be packed compactly where the service offers an appropriate method, but any claimed freight saving depends on the final route and measured parcel. Keep protective requirements separate from the desire to reduce volume. Return to the hoodie category for alternatives if the current item does not meet your fit needs. A repeatable measurement record is more valuable than a blanket claim that all Hipobuy hoodies run small. It lets you make a decision from the particular garment and the evidence available for that order.

sources.label: Nike official men’s tops size chart: body measurement definitions

title: Hipobuy Sneaker Sizing: EU, US and Insole Measurements
description: Separate shoe labels, foot length and insole measurements, then inspect both shoes before approving a warehouse order.
dek: Separate shoe labels, foot length and insole measurements, then inspect both shoes before approving a warehouse order.

sections.heading: Treat the size label as a starting point
paragraphs: Hipobuy sneaker sizing depends on the exact listing and version you select. An EU or US label is a useful starting point, but it is not a universal promise of fit across brands, models or sellers. The shape of the shoe, available width and internal construction can matter as much as a nominal size. Begin with your own measurements and a comparable pair that fits. Keep the chosen listing and size chart together so evidence from another model does not accidentally become the basis for this order.

Before paying, establish which size system the selector uses. US men's, US women's, UK and EU labels are distinct systems. A number without its system can be ambiguous, especially when a catalogue combines adult and youth options. Do not infer the intended system from your location or from the first number visible in a photograph. Check the selected option, chart and written order note. If these disagree, resolve the discrepancy first. A clear record of the requested size is essential when you later compare the received label at the warehouse.

sections.heading: Measure both feet consistently
paragraphs: Measure your feet on a firm, flat surface using a method appropriate to the chart you intend to follow. Record the heel-to-toe distance and repeat the measurement for the other foot. A helper can reduce errors caused by bending and shifting your weight while trying to mark the endpoint. Keep the paper and measuring tool stable, and write down the unit. Small differences between measurements should prompt a careful repeat rather than an immediate jump to a different shoe size.

Official fitting instructions can help you understand the method, but they apply to the chart and products described by that brand. Nike's official footwear guide distinguishes measured foot length from the CM size printed on labels and boxes. That is an important reason not to treat every number followed by cm as the same measurement. Use the corresponding chart for the exact product when it is available. A seller's claim that a model follows another brand's sizing should be treated as a claim to verify, not as a substitute for useful evidence about the received pair.

sections.heading: Keep foot length, insole length and outsole length separate
paragraphs: Foot length describes your foot. Insole length describes a removable or visible component inside a shoe. Outsole length describes the exterior bottom. These measurements answer different questions and should not be substituted for one another. An outsole can extend beyond the usable interior. An insole can curve upward or have edges that do not represent the space your foot occupies. A photograph of the sole next to a ruler therefore cannot automatically determine the correct size for your foot.

If a removable insole can be measured without damage, request a view that shows its full length and the tape endpoints. State whether the tape should follow a curve or use a straight line, then compare with a reference measured the same way. Do not prescribe one universal extra centimetre allowance for every sneaker. Toe shape, socks, intended activity and personal fit preferences vary. Treat the measurement as additional evidence alongside the label, chart and comparable footwear. Where the construction prevents a reliable measurement, acknowledge that limit instead of converting an uncertain photograph into a precise recommendation.

sections.heading: Compare the relevant dimensions of a familiar pair
paragraphs: Choose reference footwear with a similar purpose and shape. A roomy casual sneaker may not be a useful comparison for a narrow performance shoe. Record the model, marked size, width designation if present and how it fits you. Note whether your concern is toe pressure, heel movement, forefoot width or overall length. A general statement that a pair feels small is less useful than a description of where it does not fit. These notes help identify the evidence you need from the new listing.

For an illustrative comparison, suppose two removable insoles have the same measured length but different widths near the forefoot. The identical length does not make their shoes equivalent. Likewise, two shoes with the same EU label can have different internal shapes. Do not invent a new conversion table from these observations. Instead, ask whether the exact variation has a chart or measurement that addresses your concern. If the listing offers no meaningful information and returns are difficult, the uncertainty itself belongs in your purchase decision. You do not have to turn every attractive photograph into an order.

sections.heading: Verify both shoes when the pair arrives
paragraphs: Begin warehouse QC with identity checks. Compare the order record, selected colour, version and size labels on both shoes. A matching box label is not enough if the individual shoes are labelled differently. Request a photograph of each label if the standard pictures do not show them. Check that the received pair matches the chosen option rather than another style from a multi-option listing. Keep the product ID visible in your saved notes so photographs from different orders are not confused.

Then inspect the pair together from useful angles: front, back, outer sides, inner sides and soles where available. Look for visible damage, large asymmetry, loose components, unusual marks or missing included accessories. Compare like-for-like angles before judging shape. A shoe positioned closer to the camera can appear larger. Ask for a clearer view if perspective makes a material difference difficult to assess. Photographs can document visible construction and identity, but they cannot certify authenticity, cushioning performance, comfort or long-term durability. Those limits should remain clear even when the visual checks are satisfactory.

sections.heading: Resolve a size concern before international shipping
paragraphs: If the received label is wrong, provide the selected option and a clear photograph of the mismatch. If the label is correct but the measurement differs from the listing, describe the exact dimension and measuring method. Ask the relevant service what exchange or return options remain under the current terms. Avoid claiming a manufacturing error solely because a third-party size chart differs. A specific evidence-based request is easier to investigate than a general complaint that the size looks strange.

Keep three decisions separate: whether the seller sent the ordered option, whether the received item matches the published measurements, and whether it is likely to fit your needs. The first two concern the order evidence; the third can retain uncertainty even when the listing was accurate. Record any additional domestic delivery, service or return costs before replacing the pair. An agent's warehouse storage period does not automatically extend a seller's return window. Handle the concern while the practical choices are still available, and do not approve international dispatch merely to avoid asking for one useful measurement.

sections.heading: Plan packaging after approving the item
paragraphs: Once the pair is acceptable, decide what packaging you need. Keeping a shoe box may protect presentation and storage convenience, while removing it may alter parcel volume. Neither choice guarantees a particular freight saving or damage outcome. Ask which protective options are actually available and compare the final packed dimensions for eligible routes. Do not assume that the lightest arrangement is suitable for every shoe. Item approval and parcel protection solve different problems and deserve separate instructions.

Save the final order record, labels, measurement photos and packing choice. If you later buy a similar model, these observations will be more useful than a remembered size letter or a general comment from another buyer. Start future searches from the shoe category, then repeat the same checks for the new variation. This workflow cannot guarantee fit from a distance, but it gives each decision a clear basis. You know which numbers describe your feet, which describe the item, and which details still depend on trying the shoes on after delivery.

title: Hipobuy Jersey Sizing: Player vs Fan Versions and QC
description: Compare jersey versions, garment measurements, names, numbers and badges before approving a football or basketball jersey for shipping.
dek: Compare jersey versions, garment measurements, names, numbers and badges before approving a football or basketball jersey for shipping.

sections.heading: Identify the exact jersey before comparing sizes
paragraphs: A jersey listing can combine several teams, seasons, colours and versions under one product page. Begin by identifying the exact option you want. Record the team, season, home or away design, adult or youth range, sleeve length and any included shorts. For basketball or other sports, note the corresponding cut and set contents. A thumbnail is not a complete order specification. When several designs appear in the same gallery, make sure the selector and written order details refer to the same one.

Hipobuy jersey sizing should then be approached as a garment comparison. Size letters alone are not reliable evidence across different listings. A medium from one seller may have a different chest width and length from a medium elsewhere. Even within one listing, versions can use separate charts. Save the chart that applies to your selected option rather than whichever image appears first. If the seller cannot clarify which chart belongs to which variation, keep that uncertainty visible in your decision instead of assuming the measurements are shared by every product on the page.

sections.heading: Understand player and fan labels without overpromising
paragraphs: Player and fan are commonly used shopping terms, but their meaning must be checked for each listing. An official performance jersey may use different construction, fabric or fit from another retail version. That does not establish the specifications of an unrelated third-party item using similar terminology. An authentic label on a manufacturer page describes that manufacturer's product range; it is not evidence that a catalogue item with the same word is officially licensed. Judge the actual listing and evidence independently.

Do not assume that every player version is tighter, that every fan version is loose, or that a higher price proves better materials. Read the stated cut, fabric information, badge construction and measurements for the exact option. Official product pages can illustrate why versions differ, but cannot substitute for the selected seller's chart. If a listing uses several version names without explaining them, ask what physically changes. A useful answer identifies measurable differences or included features. A vague statement that one version is premium does not tell you whether it will fit or meet your requirements.

sections.heading: Compare with a jersey you already wear
paragraphs: Choose a reference jersey whose fit you know. Lay it flat without stretching and record chest width and body length using clear endpoints. Add sleeve length or shoulder width when they matter to the design. A sleeveless basketball jersey has different openings and proportions from a football shirt, so use a comparable garment where possible. Photograph your measurement method. That makes it easier to explain a request for warehouse measurements and avoids comparing a front-length measurement with a seller's longer back-length figure.

Decide how you intend to wear the jersey. Wearing it over another layer may call for different room from wearing it directly against the skin. This is a preference to compare against actual dimensions, not a reason to choose a fixed number of sizes larger. Body measurements and garment measurements are different. Check the chart's definitions before using either. Do not assume that a flat chest width represents half of the body measurement recommended by the seller. Construction, ease and the chosen style affect the relationship, and a clear product-specific chart is more useful than a universal rule.

sections.heading: Use a worked comparison to expose trade-offs
paragraphs: Imagine that a reference shirt measures 54 cm across the chest and 72 cm along the body using your chosen method. Candidate A is listed at 53 cm and 74 cm; candidate B at 56 cm and 70 cm. Candidate A is narrower and longer, while candidate B is wider and shorter. Neither is simply the next size up in every direction. These numbers are an illustrative exercise, not measurements of a listed product or a recommendation for a particular body shape.

Compare each dimension separately and note the seller's stated tolerance if available. If the preferred candidate is close to your minimum acceptable width, a warehouse measurement can be more useful than another generic front photograph. If body length matters most, request that dimension explicitly. Keep the candidate's version and size beside every measurement. A chart for a fan option should not silently become evidence for a player option. When two candidates address different needs, choose the trade-off you actually want rather than averaging measurements into a size recommendation that neither garment supports.

sections.heading: Confirm names, numbers, badges and customisation
paragraphs: Customisation creates another layer of order details. Check the spelling, accents, number, placement and any sleeve badges or competition patches you selected. Save the submitted text and the seller's description of what is included. A photograph of a famous player's shirt may illustrate the design without proving that the same name set is included in the base price. If the order has a separate customisation field or paid option, verify that it was completed correctly before assuming the finished jersey will match the example image.

Ask about the applicable cancellation, exchange and return conditions before ordering a customised item. Do not promise that a printing error, a fit problem and a change of preference will all receive the same remedy. Their treatment depends on the relevant terms and evidence. At the warehouse, compare the received lettering with the saved instruction, not with a different season's photograph. Check whether the name and number align sensibly and whether visible edges are lifting. A static image can reveal some defects, but it cannot prove how a print will perform after repeated washing.

sections.heading: Inspect the received garment in a consistent order
paragraphs: First confirm identity: selected team, design, colour, version, size and included pieces. Then inspect the useful measurements. Continue with front and back views, collar, sleeve openings, seams, crest, sponsor print and customisation where present. Look for visible marks, pulled threads, holes or large alignment differences. If the garment is folded, ask for a flat view of the area that matters. Perspective and uneven lighting can make a small difference look larger, so obtain a clear comparison before drawing a firm conclusion.

Separate what photographs show from what they cannot establish. Pictures may document a label and visible fabric texture, but they do not certify fibre composition, official licensing or performance properties. They also cannot guarantee comfort during exercise. If an important detail is missing, request targeted evidence rather than approving because the overall design looks familiar. Keep the order record and image together when reporting a mismatch. A concise explanation of the selected option and the observed difference gives support a better basis for action than an unsupported claim that the entire product is wrong.

sections.heading: Close the order with a usable record
paragraphs: Before international shipping, mark the jersey as approved, awaiting evidence or requiring an exchange or return request. Do not mix these states within a parcel merely because some items are ready. Save the final measurements and customisation photographs. If several jerseys look similar, label the records with their individual order IDs and selected options. This prevents confusion when you review a team collection or compare a later purchase. Keep any applicable deadlines separate from the broader warehouse storage period.

For packing, avoid instructions that assume all prints or trims tolerate the same treatment. Follow the item's actual care information after delivery and keep unsupported material claims out of your expectations. Return to the jersey category for a different candidate if the current option cannot meet your fit requirements. A good jersey shortlist connects each design to its own chart, measurements and order details. It gives you a practical way to compare player and fan options without pretending that those labels alone determine size, quality or authenticity.
